Samples with boron-free (0B), 0.03 at.% boron (0.03B), 0.30 at.% boron (0.30B) and 1.00 at.% boron (1.00B) were manufactured by using arc-melting in a Ti-gettered argon atmosphere.

The as-cast bars were subjected to initial solution treatment at 1200 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching to ensure a homogeneous microstructure. Subsequently, the alloy bars were thermomechanically treated using the phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) method. For further strengthening, the PSR alloy plates were cold-rolled by 30 % and aged at 700 °C for 3 h (abbreviated as PSRA).

evidence.section: 4.3 Strengthening of boron in high-temperature strength
evidence.quote: The high-temperature strengthening effect of boron element can be attributed to three possible factors: interstitial solid solution strengthening, boride precipitation strengthening, and boundary cohesion strengthened by boron.

Accompanied by the boron-strengthened phase boundary, sustainable dynamic recovery occurs in the FCC and B2 phases during high-temperature tensile testing, ensuring excellent ductility.

evidence.section: 4.2 Contribution to yield strength of FCC precipitates
evidence.quote: Since the interface between FCC precipitates and B2 matrix is semi-coherent, the strengthening effect of FCC can be estimated by the Orowan bypass mechanism
Therefore, the borides can still contribute significantly to the high-temperature yield strength of the EHEAs through Orowan strengthening mechanism.
After aging, M 3 B 2 borides precipitate along the boundaries, which can inhibit the boundary sliding during high-temperature deformation.
The boron-strengthened boundaries enable the sustainable dynamic recovery process in both FCC and B2 phases, leading to significantly enhanced 800 ◦C elongation compared with boron-free alloy.
Boron exhibits low solubility in the FCC and BCC matrices relative to boundaries, leading to its preferential diffusion and segregation at boundaries
the minor addition of boron in Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 eutectic high-entropy alloy can significantly strengthen the FCC grain boundaries and the FCC/B2 phase boundaries at elevated temperatures.

A remarkable tensile yield strength over 581 MPa with elongation of 71 % at 800 °C is achieved with minor boron addition, corresponding to a 45 % increase in yield strength and 129 % improvement in ductility compared with the boron-free counterpart.
